question.text: A mutual fund scheme has an AUM of Rs. 3,000 crore. It qualifies for an additional 30 basis points (bps) TER for B30 city inflows. How much additional annual expense (in absolute terms) can the scheme charge due to this B30 benefit?

explanation.text: The Logic: The question is a basis-points arithmetic exercise. Treating the hypothetical 30 bps additional TER as a generic rate: Additional expense = AUM x 30 bps = Rs. 3,000 crore x 0.30% = Rs. 3,000 crore x 0.003 = Rs. 9.00 crore. (1 bps = 0.01%.) The Trap: Rs. 90.00 crore uses 3% instead of 0.30% (confusing 30 bps with 30%); Rs. 0.90 crore uses 0.03% (confusing 30 bps with 3 bps); Rs. 30.00 crore applies 1% or a flat figure. Cross-Exam Context: NOTE on the regulatory claim: the current NISM V-A workbook describes additional commission/incentives for onboarding new individual investors from B-30 cities and women investors as specified by SEBI from time to time, rather than the older "fixed 30 bps additional TER for B-30 inflows" framing. Treat the 30 bps in the stem as a generic illustrative rate, not as the current B-30 TER rule.
